private-use-only.systemIntroContext: For private use, what matters is the property's condition between visits and readiness before you or your family arrive.

contrast.intro: The difference between an unchecked empty property and fixed local presence while you are away.
contrast.left1: Between visits, no one checks the property on a regular schedule.
contrast.left2: Moisture, smell, ventilation issues, or faults may surface only before arrival.
contrast.left3: Every entry depends on who holds keys and when someone can attend.
contrast.left4: Pre-arrival preparation is often rushed rather than planned in advance.
contrast.leftClosing: You respond once the problem already affects your arrival.
contrast.right1: The property is checked on an agreed rhythm between visits.
contrast.right2: Water, power, ventilation, and visible risks are checked on site.
contrast.right3: Keys and access are held locally under agreed control.
contrast.right4: Condition is documented and preparation can be planned before arrival.
contrast.rightClosing: You have a local point of control while you are away.

private-use-only.distinctionIntro: Sentinel maintains regular presence, visible checks, and documented readiness for a private-use property.
private-use-only.finalContext: The question is local control before arrival, not arranging everything from abroad.

regular-guest-stays.systemIntroContext: For regular guest stays, what matters is order between departures: access, cleaning, condition, and event documentation.

contrast.intro: The difference between owner-led turnover logistics and a fixed local structure on site.
contrast.left1: Cleaning, access, and readiness depend on several people without one reference point.
contrast.left2: Post-stay condition may be known late or without a full record.
contrast.left3: Each turnover repeats key, timing, and entry logistics.
contrast.left4: Operational decisions return to you between stays.
contrast.leftClosing: You remain the centre of every arrangement.
contrast.right1: Turnover between stays runs through an agreed local structure.
contrast.right2: Cleaner and technician access is coordinated and recorded.
contrast.right3: Post-stay checks create a documented reference before the next use.
contrast.right4: Damage and events are recorded, not scattered across messages.
contrast.rightClosing: Turnover becomes a process, not a chain of urgent calls.

regular-guest-stays.distinctionIntro: Sentinel handles local order between stays. It does not cover bookings, guest communication, or rental management.
regular-guest-stays.finalContext: The question is a fixed structure between stays, not your continuous operational involvement.

mixed-not-defined.systemIntroContext: When the use pattern is not yet clear, it must be described first. Scope is set after review.

contrast.intro: The difference between choosing intensity too early and classifying use before scope is fixed.
contrast.left1: The property may be treated as private-only even if guest activity begins later.
contrast.left2: Guest-support structure may be built before it is actually needed.
contrast.left3: Package choice may follow assumptions rather than actual use.
contrast.left4: Access, cleaning, and documentation are agreed case by case.
contrast.leftClosing: An unclear model creates the wrong basis for decisions.
contrast.right1: Actual use is reviewed before operational intensity is fixed.
contrast.right2: Private-use risk and guest-stay risk are separated before scope is confirmed.
contrast.right3: Guest-support elements are not added prematurely.
contrast.right4: Final scope follows review, not an online guess.

mixed-not-defined.distinctionIntro: Sentinel helps define how the property is used before operational intensity is chosen.
mixed-not-defined.finalContext: This is not a third pricing mode. The next step is structured review and classification.

exposure.title: What do you really risk without local representation?
exposure.p1: When you are not on site, you lose ongoing control over your home.
exposure.p2: Small problems do not make noise. They grow when no one checks.
exposure.p3: You find out about them when you are 1500 km away — without keys and without the ability to react immediately.
exposure.p4: A few days of delay is enough for a minor fault to become a serious cost.
exposure.close1: It is not about whether something will happen.
exposure.close2: It is that you will find out too late.

contrast.title: Without us / With us
contrast.intro: Below is the difference between no local representation and fixed control on site.
contrast.left1: The property isn't checked regularly while you're away.
contrast.left2: You learn about a problem when someone notices it — not when it starts.
contrast.left3: Every situation begins with logistics: who can go, who has keys, who has time.
contrast.left4: You make decisions remotely, without the full picture.
contrast.left5: Contractors act, but there is no stable reference for the property's condition.
contrast.left6: Coordination responsibility stays on your side.
contrast.leftClosing: The response starts with arranging things.
contrast.right1: The property is kept clean and prepared for your return or your guests.
contrast.right2: It's checked regularly on an agreed schedule.
contrast.right3: Its condition is documented and compared over time.
contrast.right4: Keys and access are on-site — no improvisation.
contrast.right5: When something happens, the response starts with action.
contrast.right6: Within the agreed limit, a decision can be made immediately.
contrast.right7: Responsibility and scope are defined in advance.

systemIntro.title: How the Sentinel system works
systemIntro.intro: Sentinel provides fixed, local control over your property.
systemIntro.scope1: Scope of action is clearly defined — you know what is checked and how often.
systemIntro.scope2: You have a transparent operating model based on fixed rules.
systemIntro.procedure1: Every visit follows the same steps.
systemIntro.procedure2: The same actions, the same order, the same control.
systemIntro.procedure3: You know the actual state of your home, not an approximate picture.
systemIntro.docs1: After each inspection you receive documentation: photos, description, and a record of changes over time.
systemIntro.docs2: You have continuity of information and the ability to compare property condition over time.
systemIntro.decisions1: We act when the situation requires it.
systemIntro.decisions2a: Thanks to local presence we can act immediately —
systemIntro.decisions2b: whether on technical matters or access for you and your guests.
systemIntro.decisions3: We take action without unnecessary delay.

levels.title: Package scope
levels.intro: Choosing a package defines the scope of local control.
levels.level1_6: Limitations: no access coordination; no autonomous decisions.
levels.level2_1: Organisation and supervision of third-party access
levels.level2_2: Access documentation and initial repair coordination
levels.level3_2: Decisions within limit (€300 / €500) and extended work coordination
levels.level3_6: Limitations: above limit owner approval is required.
levels.systemRule1: Scope is determined solely by the chosen package.
levels.systemRule2: Services not listed are not included.
levels.systemRule3: Every action is subject to documentation.

distinction.title: What distinguishes Sentinel
distinction.block1p1: The scope of cooperation is defined before work begins. Each property goes through a qualification process before cooperation starts.
distinction.block1p2: Specific people deliver the work under the same rules. We operate within agreed frameworks, not ad hoc.
distinction.block2p1: Occasional help reacts when a problem appears. We operate to a schedule and procedure.
distinction.block2p2: That makes it possible to spot situations earlier, not only when they become costly.
distinction.block3p1: Every visit leaves a record: photos, description, date, scope of actions. Operational events are recorded together with decisions taken.
distinction.block3p2: You have an action history and condition comparison over time. It is based on record, not memory.
distinction.block4p1: When a situation requires a response, it is clear:
distinction.block4p2: Events outside the agreed scope require separate agreement. Agreement precedes action.
distinction.block4p3: There is no improvisation or guesswork. Responsibility is clearly assigned.
distinction.block5p1: The model defines the structure. People are responsible for execution.
distinction.block5p2: Fixed rules keep the standard; personal responsibility means actions are not anonymous.
distinction.block5p3: The team has over 25 years of technical experience.
distinction.block5p4: That combination gives stability that informal help does not provide.

differentiation.title: Why this model is not concierge or rental management
differentiation.concierge1: The concierge model relies on flexible scope, with no fixed boundaries of responsibility.
differentiation.concierge2: Scope expands with each new situation.
differentiation.sentinelScope: Sentinel operates only within predefined levels of involvement. Scope is defined before cooperation begins.
differentiation.rental1: Rental management focuses on guests and operational revenue.
differentiation.rental2: Owner representation is not the priority.
differentiation.adhoc1: One-off local help does not create a system or a history of changes.
differentiation.adhoc2: No system means no fixed point of control.
differentiation.modelBasis: The model is not based on personal relationship. It is based on operational repeatability.

principles.title: Operational principles
principles.intro: The system operates within defined boundaries.
principles.introWhy: Boundaries exist so that responsibility is unambiguous.
principles.rule1: Every action is documented and archived.
principles.rule1b: Documentation provides a fixed reference point for property condition.
principles.rule2: Scope of action is determined solely by the chosen level of involvement.
principles.rule2b: Scope does not expand automatically with new situations.
principles.rule3: Financial authority has a defined limit.
principles.rule3b: The limit defines the scope of independent operational decisions.
principles.rule4: Events outside the agreed scope require separate agreement.
principles.rule5: Area of operation is fixed (Torrevieja + 50–70 km radius).

serviceArea.title: Area of operation
serviceArea.subtitle: Fixed operational jurisdiction
serviceArea.intro: Sentinel operates only in Torrevieja and within a 50–70 km radius.
serviceArea.introNote1: The geographic boundary is not a marketing element.
serviceArea.close: Jurisdiction remains fixed to maintain responsibility and operational standard.

capacity.title: Operational capacity
capacity.intro: The system is built on documented onboarding procedures.
capacity.item1: Each property goes through qualification and scope configuration.
capacity.item2: After each visit a photo report is produced.
capacity.item3: Operational events are recorded together with decisions taken.
capacity.item4: Execution takes place through ongoing cooperation with local contractors.
capacity.item5: The team has over 25 years of technical experience.

finalCta.title: You can manage reactively. Or operate within the system.
finalCta.p1: Reactive management is based on reacting. The system is based on steady control.
finalCta.p2: Sentinel is a defined model of owner representation. The choice is about the structure of local oversight and owner representation.
finalCta.cta: Verify whether your property qualifies for the Sentinel system

meta.title: Service Packages - Sentinel
meta.description: Scope and responsibility of Sentinel service packages

intro.headline: Service Packages — Scope and Responsibility
intro.lead1: Sentinel operates on three levels of involvement.
intro.lead2: They differ in scope of responsibility, access coordination, and decision authority. If a service is not explicitly included in a package, it is not part of its scope.
intro.engagementTerms: Minimum commitment: 3 months. Monthly billing in advance.

hero.headline: Choose the level of local responsibility
hero.lead: The package defines how often Sentinel is on site, how access is handled, and where decisions stop without additional owner approval.

ladder.title: Packages differ by operating depth, not by a random list of add-ons.
ladder.intro: First you choose the level of oversight. Visit rhythm, access, readiness cleaning, or event support are then confirmed inside that level.

basic.responsibility: Regular presence, property condition, and basic visit record.
basic.fit: For a property used mainly privately, where the owner needs scheduled checks but keeps most decisions.

extended.responsibility: More active checks, third-party access, and event coordination.
extended.fit: For a property with technicians, cleaning, guests, or local work that requires controlled handling.

full.responsibility: Operational priority and broader decisions inside the agreed limit.
full.fit: For an owner who wants fewer remote decisions and a higher response priority.

scenario.title: Which situation sounds most like your property?
scenario.intro: This is not the homepage pathway gate and it does not change the URL. It only helps identify which package level to review first.
scenario.note: This fit is educational. Final scope is confirmed after structured review of the property.

private.label: Empty property
private.title: The apartment is empty between owner visits
private.body: The main need is scheduled checks, key access, and a documented condition record.
private.result: Basic is usually the starting point when there is no regular guest traffic or frequent third-party entry.

guest.label: Activity and access
guest.title: Guests, cleaning, or technicians enter regularly
guest.body: The risk is not only property condition, but access coordination and event documentation.
guest.result: Extended is often required because condition checks alone do not cover regular access events.

decisions.label: Local decisions
decisions.title: You do not want to handle every small decision remotely
decisions.body: The property needs a decision limit, faster response, and a clear owner approval boundary.
decisions.result: Full is a closer fit when the central need is decision handling within a defined limit.

mixed.label: Unclear model
mixed.title: The future use pattern is not fixed yet
mixed.body: The first step is classification, not choosing the heaviest scope too early.
mixed.result: Extended can be a reference point for discussion, but mixed use starts with classification.

events.title: See how the scope works in a concrete event.
events.intro: These scenarios explain operating logic. They do not create new promises or authority outside the package.

leak.label: Moisture / valve
leak.title: Moisture is spotted during a visit
leak.lead: The first task is observation, documented evidence, and action inside agreed authority.
leak.observes: Visible valve condition, moisture traces, and risk of further damage.
leak.documents: Photos, location notes, visit time, and recommended next action.
leak.owner: Approval is required when action exceeds the limit or package scope.
leak.package: A higher package means faster handling and a higher decision limit, not a guarantee that the cause is resolved.

technician.label: Technician entry
technician.title: A technician needs access to the property
technician.lead: Access follows agreed rules, not improvised key handover.
technician.observes: The purpose of entry, the access request, and whether it sits inside the agreed scope.
technician.documents: Entry time, person or role, presence scope, and condition after the visit.
technician.owner: The owner approves work, cost, or scope beyond prior agreement.
technician.package: Extended and Full handle recurring access events better than condition-only oversight.

turnover.label: Readiness after cleaning
turnover.title: The property needs to be ready after guest use
turnover.lead: Sentinel does not become a cleaning company, but can handle readiness and documentation inside agreed scope.
turnover.observes: Visible entry condition, basic readiness, and items requiring follow-up.
turnover.documents: Reference photos, noted gaps, and whether further action is required.
turnover.owner: Extra work, cost, or rhythm changes remain subject to approval.
turnover.package: Regular guest activity usually points toward Extended or Full.

weekend.label: Urgent signal
weekend.title: An urgent issue appears outside the normal rhythm
weekend.lead: SLA defines response and decision timing, not guaranteed third-party repair time.
weekend.observes: Event priority, access availability, and whether securing action is required.
weekend.documents: The notice, action taken within limit, and items awaiting owner decision.
weekend.owner: The owner approves action beyond the limit, higher cost, or extra work.
weekend.package: Full has the highest priority while still operating inside package limits and real contractor availability.

packageDetails.eyebrow: Scope without the wall of text
packageDetails.title: One panel, one level of responsibility.
packageDetails.intro: Details remain one click away, while the essential differences stay visible immediately.
packageDetails.fullScopeExplainer: The expansion preserves important package substance without repeating it as three large articles.

boundary.title: Sentinel acts locally, but only inside the agreed scope.
boundary.intro: The main boundaries appear before the estimator. The full legal wording remains in the terms and package detail.

oversight.title: Local oversight
oversight.body: Scheduled condition checks and a record of what is visible on site.

access.title: Controlled access
access.body: Keyholding or access handling according to the agreement and package.

documentation.title: Event documentation
documentation.body: Reports, photos, notes, and indication of required owner decision.

coordination.title: Operational coordination
coordination.body: Contact with technician, cleaning, or contractor inside the agreed scope.

rentalAgency.title: Rental agency
rentalAgency.body: Sentinel does not handle bookings, pricing, licensing, or platform communication.

concierge.title: Concierge
concierge.body: No lifestyle services, unlimited favors, or tasks without defined scope.

unlimitedEmergency.title: Unlimited emergency contractor
unlimitedEmergency.body: Decisions and costs have limits; repairs depend on available contractors.

undefinedTasks.title: Undefined tasks
undefinedTasks.body: Anything outside the package or agreement requires separate approval.

modules.title: Modules help execute the scope. They do not create a fourth package.
modules.intro: Keys, cleaning, readiness, and technician entry are practical functions inside the agreed oversight system.

estimatorBand.title: First identify the responsibility level, then calculate an indicative range.

details.frameworkExplainer: Visit scheduling, decision limits, communication, and billing stay available without dominating the page.
details.notIncludedExplainer: Exclusions are part of the responsibility boundary, not a separate offer.

escalation.title: Three oversight levels
escalation.intro: The package level defines the authorised scope: control, access, and decision handling inside agreed limits.
escalation.footerNote: Decision handling remains bounded by the selected package, emergency authority, and documented owner approvals.

meta.title: How It Works - Sentinel
meta.description: Complete onboarding process from initial contact to active service

intro.headline: How Sentinel Service Works
intro.description: Sentinel follows a structured onboarding process to ensure clear understanding, proper documentation, and operational readiness before service activation. This page outlines each step from initial contact to active service. Service is not activated until onboarding is complete.
intro.processOverview: The process consists of: Qualification → Package Selection → Property Documentation → Initial Inspection → Service Activation. Timeline depends on property availability and documentation completion.

hero.headline: From first contact to documented oversight
hero.lead: The process does not start with an open task list. Property, access, scope, and reporting are confirmed first.

timeline.title: Agreement first. Then presence, report, and decisions.

before.title: Before service
before.body: Sentinel qualifies the property, operating area, and how the property is used.

setup.title: Access setup
setup.body: Keys, data, package, scope, and communication rules are confirmed.

active.title: Active oversight
active.body: Visits, entries, and events are handled according to the selected package.

followup.title: Report and decision
followup.body: The owner receives documentation and a clear indication of where approval is required.

oneMinute.title: Four things must be clear before Sentinel starts acting.
oneMinute.intro: This short version follows the order in which a remote owner usually understands the process.

qualify.title: Qualify the property
qualify.body: Address, property type, operating area, and use pattern must fit the Sentinel model.

scope.title: Agree scope and access
scope.body: Package, keys, contact people, and entry rules are confirmed before activation.

inspect.title: Inspect and document
inspect.body: The first inspection creates the baseline condition and reporting structure.

escalate.title: Report and escalate
escalate.body: Sentinel acts inside the limit. Above the limit, the owner decides.

storyboard.title: What happens during a typical visit
storyboard.intro: A visit is not a general look around. It is a sequence of access, checks, documentation, and report.

arrive.title: Arrive at the building
arrive.body: Sentinel arrives according to the rhythm or an agreed event.

access.title: Controlled access
access.body: Keys and entry follow rules confirmed in advance.

check.title: Risk points
check.body: Visible access, water, electrical, moisture, and interior condition points are checked.

document.title: Photos and notes
document.body: Condition and events are recorded in a useful form for the owner.

report.title: Remote report
report.body: The owner receives a summary, photos, and next-step information.

decision.title: Decision boundary
decision.body: If action exceeds limit or scope, owner approval is required.

report.title: The report shows what was observed and what needs a decision.
report.intro: The report appears before long process detail because it shows the mechanism: observation, documentation, status, and next action.

summary.title: Summary
summary.body: Short visit status and whether an issue was identified.

checklist.title: Checklist
checklist.body: Visible risk points are recorded in a consistent structure.

photos.title: Reference photos
photos.body: Images show elements relevant to condition, access, or event context.

q1.question: Can I start immediately without full onboarding?
q1.answer: No. Service is activated only after complete onboarding. This protects both parties.

q2.question: What if I don't have all information yet?
q2.answer: Onboarding will pause until required information is provided. Service cannot begin with incomplete data.

q3.question: Can I change my package during onboarding?
q3.answer: Yes, before activation. After activation, package changes require new agreement.

q4.question: What if the initial inspection reveals problems?
q4.answer: Issues are documented in the initial report. Client decides whether to address them before service begins or accept property "as is" with documented baseline.

q5.question: Do I pay before or after activation?
q5.answer: Payment terms are specified during package confirmation (Step 2). Service activation may require initial payment or deposit as per agreed terms.

q6.question: Can someone else be present during initial inspection?
q6.answer: Yes, if arranged in advance. Not required.

q7.question: What if I need to delay activation after onboarding?
q7.answer: Discuss with Sentinel. If activation is delayed significantly after onboarding, a re-check may be required before service starts to confirm the baseline condition remains accurate.

serviceModel.title: Service Model & Packages
serviceModel.description: Questions about Sentinel's service structure, package boundaries, and what is/isn't included.

q1.question: What exactly is Sentinel?
q1.answer: Sentinel is a local property representation service operating on package-based contracts with defined scope. Services include physical presence, inspection, coordination, and reporting within explicitly defined package boundaries—not concierge or unlimited assistance. Review Services page for complete package specifications; if your needs don't align with package structure, Sentinel may not be appropriate.

q2.question: Can I order a single visit without a package?
q2.answer: No. Sentinel operates exclusively on monthly package basis to ensure service continuity and operational accountability. If you need one-time assistance, contact a local contractor or agency; Sentinel can only engage after onboarding under a monthly package.

q3.question: What if I need something not in my package?
q3.answer: Services outside your package are quoted separately and require written approval before execution. Sentinel does not perform "small favors" or undocumented services; all work outside package scope must be formally arranged and priced. Contact Sentinel with specific request; you will receive quote and can approve, decline, or upgrade package if recurring need exists.

q4.question: Can you let in a cleaner or technician if I have Basic package?
q4.answer: No. Basic package does not include third-party access coordination; this requires Extended or Full package. Upgrade to Extended package for access coordination, or arrange access yourself and maintain Basic for inspection-only service.

q5.question: What exactly is an "access event"?
q5.answer: Every opening and closing of the property for a third party counts as one access event, regardless of duration. Access event includes travel, unlocking, supervision, securing, and brief report—whether visit lasts 15 minutes or 3 hours. Extended includes 2 events/month; additional events are billed separately. Full includes fair-use access (reasonable operational frequency).

q6.question: Can I ask for entry "just for a moment"?
q6.answer: No—brief visits still count as access events. Duration does not affect access event classification; operational cost (travel, coordination, securing) is identical regardless of time on-site. Plan access needs appropriately within package allocation, or move to Extended or Full package for fair-use access without strict monthly limits.

operations.title: Operations & Scheduling
operations.description: Questions about visit timing, technician coordination, and operational windows.

q7.question: What if a technician arrives "between 9 AM and 2 PM"?
q7.answer: Sentinel operates within time windows, not fixed appointments. Long on-site waiting for technicians is not included in Basic or Extended packages; Full package includes on-site presence during service visits. Basic/Extended clients coordinate technician timing themselves; Full clients receive on-site supervision as part of package.

q8.question: Do you react immediately to every request?
q8.answer: No—response time depends on package SLA (Service Level Agreement). SLA defines reaction and decision time, not guaranteed resolution time; Basic acknowledges within 48h, Extended within 24h, Full follows same-day response discipline. Review package SLA commitments on Services page; external factors (technician availability, parts) affect actual resolution beyond Sentinel's control.

emergencies.title: Emergencies & Decision Authority
emergencies.description: Questions about emergency response, decision-making authority, and financial limits.

q9.question: What is considered an emergency?
q9.answer: Events causing or threatening immediate material damage, property loss, or safety hazard. Emergencies include active leaks, broken security, fire damage, gas leaks, electrical hazards—NOT WiFi issues, comfort problems, or guest complaints. Full package includes emergency response; Basic/Extended receive emergency action only after owner approval or if property securing is immediately necessary (€300 limit).

q10.question: What happens in emergency if I don't answer phone?
q10.answer: Sentinel takes property-securing action up to €300 limit if owner is unreachable and threat is immediate. All packages include limited emergency securing authority when immediate property threat exists and owner contact fails; all actions documented and reported. Provide reliable emergency contact information during onboarding; Full package clients receive immediate action within approved decision limit (€300-500).

q11.question: What is the decision limit in Full package?
q11.answer: Standard limit is €300 per single decision; optional increase to €500 can be specified during onboarding. Limit applies per individual decision (not cumulative monthly); decisions above limit require owner approval before action. Specify preferred limit during onboarding; Sentinel will not exceed approved limit without explicit permission.

q12.question: Do you take financial responsibility for damages?
q12.answer: No. Sentinel coordinates and represents but does not provide insurance-level liability or guarantee prevention of all incidents. Property owners must maintain adequate insurance coverage; Sentinel's accountability is limited to service delivery within package scope.

practical.title: Practical Operations
practical.description: Questions about day-to-day service details, visit frequency, and package changes.

q13.question: Can you store valuables?
q13.answer: Short-term storage is possible after specific arrangement; Sentinel does not assume liability for undeclared valuables. Safe storage available for documented items only; Sentinel is not responsible for valuables not explicitly declared and logged. Discuss specific storage needs during onboarding; ensure adequate insurance coverage for stored items.

q14.question: Can you take care of animals?
q14.answer: Short-term animal care is possible after advance arrangement; regular pet care is not part of any package. Occasional brief animal supervision can be arranged separately; Sentinel does not provide ongoing pet care services. Contact Sentinel with specific needs; permanent pet care requires separate local arrangement.

q15.question: Do you check utility meters?
q15.answer: Yes—Basic includes visual check or reading as agreed during onboarding; Extended/Full include reading and photos. Meter inspection method is specified during onboarding; format and frequency depend on package and property access. Confirm meter inspection preferences during onboarding; photos available if meters are accessible.

q16.question: Can I have only one visit per month?
q16.answer: Standard is 2 visits/month; less frequent visits require individual arrangement and may affect service scope. Reduced visit frequency increases risk and may limit Sentinel's accountability; any deviation from standard schedule must be explicitly agreed. Discuss reduced frequency during onboarding; understand that longer intervals between visits reduce early problem detection.

q17.question: Can I change my package during cooperation?
q17.answer: Yes—package changes are possible at any time upon mutual agreement. Changes require written confirmation of new package terms and take effect from agreed date (typically next billing period). Contact Sentinel to discuss package upgrade/downgrade; new terms documented before change activation.

q18.question: Do you support properties with regular guest stays?
q18.answer: Not as primary service—rental support is available only as add-on module to existing package. Sentinel does not provide full property management, guest communication, or booking services; rental support covers only property preparation and post-departure inspection. Review Rental/Holiday Support add-on module on Services page; requires base package (Basic, Extended, or Full) plus separate arrangement.

communication.title: Communication & Policies
communication.description: Questions about how to contact Sentinel, policy changes, and service refusal.

q19.question: How does communication work?
q19.answer: Operational communication via dedicated phone/WhatsApp; formal documentation via email. Sentinel maintains separate channels for prospects (general contact) and active clients (dedicated operational line); no communication through personal team numbers. Use contact form or general number for initial inquiry; active clients receive dedicated contact information during onboarding.

q20.question: Can you refuse cooperation?
q20.answer: Yes—Sentinel reserves right to decline service or terminate cooperation. Sentinel may refuse service if property is outside service area, expectations don't align with package model, or operational fit is not viable. Qualification occurs before onboarding; Sentinel evaluates property location, service needs, and client expectations before accepting engagement.

q21.question: Can prices and terms change?
q21.answer: Yes, but changes are communicated in advance and apply from next billing period (not retroactively). Sentinel may adjust pricing or terms with advance notice; existing clients receive notification before changes take effect. Changes do not affect current billing period; clients can accept new terms or terminate service at end of current period.

q22.question: What if something isn't described in the documentation?
q22.answer: If not explicitly listed, it's not included in the package. Services, procedures, and commitments exist only as documented; undocumented services require separate arrangement and approval. Legal and regulatory compliance for the property remains the sole responsibility of the owner. Contact Sentinel with specific request; anything outside documented package scope will be quoted separately.

q23.question: Why are there so many rules?
q23.answer: Rules protect both parties by defining scope, preventing disputes, and enabling accountability. Documentation ensures service delivery doesn't depend on individual interpretation or goodwill; clear boundaries enable reliable, professional service. Review Services and How It Works pages to understand operational framework; rules exist to support long-term service quality.

meta.title: Meta / Purpose of Rules
meta.description: Questions about where these policies apply and why this documentation exists.

q24.question: Where do these policies apply?
q24.answer: Policies apply to all Sentinel operations: website, communications, service agreements, and client relations. No verbal agreements or informal exceptions override documented policies; all service terms must be explicitly agreed and documented. Acceptance of documented policies is required for service activation; disagreement with policies means Sentinel is not appropriate service provider.

q25.question: What is the purpose of this FAQ document?
q25.answer: This document prevents misunderstandings, clarifies boundaries, establishes shared reference point, and protects both parties. FAQ serves as operational policy reference and dispute resolution tool; answers are consistent with service terms and package specifications. Use this FAQ as first resource for questions; contact Sentinel if your specific situation is not addressed.

meta.title: About - Sentinel
meta.description: Operational philosophy, system design, and service boundaries

intro.description: Sentinel is a local property representation service operating on a package-based model with defined scope and documented procedures. This page explains our operational philosophy, geographic focus, system design, and the operational resources that support service delivery.
intro.subtext: We do not operate on personality-driven trust or concierge flexibility. We operate on documented procedures, defined scope, and enforceable accountability.

philosophy.title: Why Package-Based Property Representation
philosophy.intro: Sentinel was designed to solve a specific operational problem: property owners living outside Spain need reliable local representation, but traditional models—key holding, concierge services, or full property management—create misaligned expectations and undefined responsibility.
philosophy.subtitle: Package-based service model exists because:

scopeClarity.title: Scope clarity prevents disputes:
scopeClarity.description: When services are defined in advance, both parties know exactly what is included and what requires separate arrangement.

procedures.title: Documented procedures enable consistency:
procedures.description: Standardized checklists, inspection protocols, and reporting ensure service quality does not depend on individual discretion.

responsibility.title: Defined responsibility protects both parties:
responsibility.description: Clear boundaries prevent scope creep, unrealistic expectations, and operational overreach.

geographic.title: Geographic focus enables accountability:
geographic.description: Limiting service area to Torrevieja + 50-70km ensures realistic response times and sustainable service quality.

philosophy.practice: What this means in practice: If a service is not explicitly listed in your package, it is not included. This is not inflexibility—it is the foundation of reliable, accountable service delivery.

geographic.title: Geographic Boundary: Operational Rationale
geographic.intro: Sentinel services properties within Torrevieja and approximately 50-70km radius. This geographic limitation is permanent and applies to all clients without exception.
geographic.subtitle: Why geographic boundaries exist:

reasons.responseTime: Response time commitments: Full package clients receive same-day response discipline within defined decision boundaries. This is only sustainable within manageable distance.
reasons.visitFrequency: Visit frequency reliability: Regular biweekly or weekly visits require proximity. Distant properties create scheduling conflicts and service degradation.
reasons.emergencyAccess: Emergency access capability: Property securing in case of active leaks, broken locks, or weather damage requires rapid physical presence.
reasons.qualityControl: Quality control: Local presence enables relationship management with cleaners, technicians, and municipal services. Distance erodes these operational relationships.
reasons.sustainability: Cost sustainability: Travel time beyond 70km makes service economically unsustainable without pricing that defeats the purpose.

geographic.footer: Properties outside this area cannot be serviced—not temporarily, not as exceptions, not at premium pricing. This boundary is designed to protect service quality for clients within the area, not to limit growth arbitrarily.

system.title: Operational System and Process Framework
system.intro: Sentinel operates on documented procedures covering all aspects of service delivery:

items.dataCollection: Complete data collection (property details, access codes, emergency contacts)
items.inspection: Initial inspection (Visit Zero) establishing baseline property condition

items.checklists: Visit checklists ensuring consistent inspection coverage
items.assessments: Meter readings, system checks, and condition assessments

items.approval: Written approval required for all access events
items.reports: Brief reports after each third-party visit

items.criteria: Defined emergency criteria (material damage, safety hazard)

items.dedicated: Dedicated operational contact lines (separate from prospect inquiries)
items.sla: Service Level Agreements (SLA) by package tier
items.formal: Formal documentation via email for decisions and changes

system.footer: What this means: Service delivery does not depend on individual judgment or goodwill. Procedures are documented, repeatable, and enforceable. This is what enables accountability.

resources.title: Operational Resources and Capacity
resources.intro: Sentinel service delivery is enabled by local operational resources and established partnerships:

items.cleaner: Dedicated cleaner with hotel industry background and property oversight experience
items.technician: Experienced technician with 25+ years in plumbing, electrical work, and construction
items.network: Local vendor network for specialized services (HVAC, pool maintenance, garden care)

items.coordinator: Operational coordinator managing client communication, scheduling, and decision-making
items.reporting: Documented reporting and photo management system
items.protocols: Emergency contact protocols and escalation procedures

items.partnership: Partnership with NowRent.eu for airport transfers and vehicle services
items.scheduling: Advance scheduling required (14+ days in summer season)
items.availability: Subject to availability and separate pricing

items.limited: Service capacity is limited by geographic focus and resource availability
items.seasonal: Seasonal demand affects scheduling flexibility (particularly June-September)
items.decline: Sentinel reserves the right to decline service when capacity limits are reached

items.contractor: Sentinel does not employ general contractors for major renovation work
items.availability: Sentinel does not provide 24/7 unlimited availability
items.individuals: Sentinel does not guarantee specific individuals for every visit

resources.footer: Operational capability exists to deliver package commitments reliably—not to provide unlimited flexibility.

notWhat.title: What Sentinel Is Not
notWhat.intro: To prevent misunderstanding, Sentinel explicitly states what it is NOT:

items.prevention: Sentinel does not guarantee prevention of all incidents
items.liability: Sentinel does not assume insurance-level liability
items.forceMajeure: Sentinel does not cover losses from force majeure events
items.coverage: Property owners remain responsible for adequate insurance coverage

items.unlimited: Sentinel does not provide unlimited personal assistance
items.errands: Sentinel does not handle errands, shopping, or lifestyle management
items.flexibility: Sentinel does not operate on "whatever you need" flexibility
items.separate: Services outside packages require separate arrangement and pricing

propertyManagement.title: Not a full property management company:

items.bookings: Sentinel does not manage bookings or guest communication (except as add-on)
items.support: Sentinel does not provide 24/7 guest support
items.agency: Sentinel does not act as rental agency or booking platform
items.addon: Rental support is available only as add-on module to core packages

items.coordinates: Sentinel coordinates repairs but does not execute construction work
items.quality: Sentinel is not liable for quality of work performed by third-party contractors
items.projects: Sentinel does not manage renovation projects
items.licensed: Specialized work requires engagement of licensed contractors

items.sla: Service Level Agreements define response times by package
items.red: Emergency response is available only to Full package clients
items.timeframes: Non-emergency requests are handled within SLA timeframes
items.guarantee: Immediate availability outside SLA is not guaranteed

notWhat.footer: Sentinel is a local property representation service operating within defined scope, documented procedures, and clear accountability boundaries.

accountability.title: Accountability Within Defined Scope

items.visits: Completing scheduled visits per package frequency
items.reports: Delivering photo reports within committed timeframes
items.sla: Responding to requests within Service Level Agreement (SLA)

items.photos: Photo documentation of all visits and access events
items.written: Written reports of observations, actions taken, and concerns identified
items.meters: Accurate meter readings and system condition notes
items.emergency: Emergency action documentation with timeline and decision rationale

items.operational: Operational decisions up to approved financial limit (€300-€500)
items.securing: Property securing actions in case of immediate threat
items.repair: Emergency repair coordination within decision authority

items.response: Response to client inquiries within SLA timeframes
items.notice: Advance notice of schedule changes or limitations
items.clarity: Clear communication when requests fall outside package scope
items.written: Written documentation of all agreements and changes

items.prevention: Guarantee of preventing all incidents or losses
items.control: Responsibility for events outside Sentinel's control (weather, municipal services, force majeure)

accountability.footer: Accountability is enforceable because scope is defined, procedures are documented, and commitments are explicit.

hero.headline: Built for owners who are not on site
hero.lead: Sentinel is Structured Property Oversight for remote owners on the southern Costa Blanca. The model exists so local presence, access, documentation, and owner decisions are handled inside a defined operating scope.

why.title: Remote ownership creates an operational gap.
why.intro: A property can be local, active, and vulnerable while the owner is far away. Informal help can solve a task, but it rarely defines responsibility.

cards.title: The owner is away
cards.body: Distance makes access, inspection, and urgent judgment difficult to manage directly.

cards.title: The property remains local
cards.body: Doors, keys, water, electricity, cleaners, technicians, and weather still require physical presence.

cards.title: Ad-hoc help has limits
cards.body: One-off favors can leave unclear records, unclear authority, and unclear accountability.

why.closing: Sentinel exists to replace informal delegation with a local operating structure: scope first, access controlled, checks documented, decisions bounded.

model.title: Credibility comes from how the work is controlled.
model.intro: The model is deliberately structured. It defines when Sentinel is present, what can be checked, how access is handled, and when a decision returns to the owner.

items.title: Local presence
items.body: Work happens inside a realistic service area, not from a distant coordination desk.

items.title: Controlled access
items.body: Keys, entry, and third-party access are used only inside the agreed scope.

items.title: Documented checks
items.body: Visits and relevant events leave a report, note, photo set, or written confirmation.

items.title: Owner decision boundary
items.body: Sentinel acts within agreed limits. Above the limit or outside scope, the owner approves.

items.title: Package scope
items.body: Responsibility increases through Basic, Extended, and Full packages without creating open-ended service.

boundary.title: What Sentinel is, and what it is not.
boundary.intro: The service is easier to trust when the category is clear. Sentinel is not positioned as flexible household help or rental operations.

isItems.title: Local oversight
isItems.body: Physical presence for agreed checks, access, and events.

isItems.title: Owner representation
isItems.body: A structured local layer acting inside the owner's confirmed scope.

isItems.title: Documentation
isItems.body: Reports, notes, photos, and confirmations after relevant activity.

isItems.title: Access coordination
isItems.body: Controlled entry for visits, technicians, cleaning, or agreed modules.

isItems.title: Structured escalation
isItems.body: Clear owner approval points when authority or scope is exceeded.

isNotItems.title: Concierge
isNotItems.body: No open-ended errands, lifestyle tasks, or undefined assistance.

isNotItems.title: Rental agency
isNotItems.body: No booking platform role or rental-business management.

isNotItems.title: General contractor
isNotItems.body: No construction execution or guarantee of third-party work quality.

isNotItems.title: Unlimited emergency service
isNotItems.body: Response and authority are defined by package and agreed limits.

isNotItems.title: Informal favor network
isNotItems.body: Work is scoped and recorded rather than improvised.

local.title: The 50-70 km boundary is an operating rule, not a marketing claim.
local.intro: Sentinel serves Torrevieja and the surrounding southern Costa Blanca area because physical presence must stay realistic.

cards.title: Travel discipline
cards.body: Visit rhythm and event response depend on manageable distance.

cards.title: Local relationships
cards.body: Cleaners, technicians, and access coordination work better inside a known area.

cards.title: Service refusal
cards.body: Out-of-area properties are declined instead of being absorbed into weak coverage.

local.note: The boundary protects service quality for properties inside the operating area.

capabilities.title: Sentinel can act because practical functions sit inside the oversight system.
capabilities.intro: Keys, cleaning readiness, access, checks, reporting, and contractor coordination are operational capabilities. They do not turn Sentinel into a cleaning company, concierge, or rental agency.

items.title: Access basis
items.body: Keys or access methods are held and used according to the agreement.

items.title: Cleaning and arrival state
items.body: Cleaning or readiness support may be included or coordinated where the scope allows it.

items.title: Technician and service entry
items.body: Entry events can be coordinated, recorded, and reported when agreed.

items.title: Visible condition review
items.body: Visits focus on observable risk points and package-defined checklist items.

items.title: Owner record
items.body: The owner receives usable documentation after visits or relevant events.

items.title: External work where agreed
items.body: Sentinel may coordinate contractors inside defined authority, but does not guarantee their work.

capabilities.note: The capability layer exists to make oversight executable. It is not an invitation to unlimited task handling.

responsibility.title: Action follows agreement, scope, documentation, and approval.
responsibility.intro: This is the operating discipline behind the service. It is intentionally less flexible than informal help.

steps.title: Agreement before action
steps.body: Property data, access method, package, and communication rules are confirmed first.

steps.title: Scope before execution
steps.body: The task must fit the package or an agreed module before Sentinel acts.

steps.title: Documentation after action
steps.body: Visits, access events, observations, and relevant decisions leave a record.

steps.title: Owner approval above limits
steps.body: Financial or operational decisions outside authority return to the owner.

responsibility.note: This is why Sentinel can be commercially useful without becoming an undefined property-management promise.

details.title: The operating logic remains available without becoming the page.
details.intro: The sections below preserve important detail for owners who need to verify fit before contact.

model.title: Package-based model
model.explainer: Why the service is structured instead of flexible.
model.body: If a service is not explicitly listed in the package or agreed module, it is not included. This protects scope clarity, pricing clarity, and responsibility boundaries.

area.title: Geographic boundary
area.body: Properties outside the operating area cannot be served as exceptions. Response time, visit rhythm, and local coordination depend on manageable distance.

accountability.title: Defined accountability
accountability.body: Accountability is enforceable because scope is defined, procedures are documented, reports are produced, and decisions above authority limits require owner approval.

cta.title: Use the About page as a fit check.
cta.intro: If the model fits your property, the next step is a structured review. If you need open-ended property management or concierge support, Sentinel is not the correct category.

sections.title: 1. Definition of Service
sections.body:
Sentinel provides a package-based local property representation service within a defined operational scope.

The service is not:

Insurance
A concierge service
A rental agency
A general contractor
Full-scope property management

sections.title: 2. Geographic Area
sections.body:
The service is provided only within Torrevieja and a 50–70 km radius.

Properties outside this area cannot be served.

sections.title: 3. Package Model
sections.body:
Services are delivered only under monthly packages:

Basic
Extended
Full

If a service is not explicitly listed in the package, it is not included.

Additional services require separate agreement and quotation.

sections.title: 4. SLA
sections.body:
SLA defines:

Response time
Decision time

SLA does not guarantee time to full resolution of an issue.

sections.title: 5. Decision Authority
sections.body:
In the Full Package a decision limit applies:

Standard: €300 per single decision
Optional: €500 (if agreed)

Decisions above the limit require owner approval.

sections.title: 6. Liability
sections.body:
Sentinel is responsible for:

Delivery of services in accordance with the package
Documentation of actions
Response in line with SLA

Sentinel is not responsible for:

Force majeure
Errors by third-party contractors
Insurance-type losses
Failure to prevent all incidents

sections.title: 7. Payments
sections.body:
The service is billed:

Monthly in advance
Minimum engagement period: 3 months

Payment may be made by:

Bank transfer
Online via the payment system

Non-payment may result in suspension or termination of the service.

sections.title: 8. Termination
sections.body:
The client may terminate the service at the end of the billing period.

Sentinel may terminate the service in case of:

Breach of scope
Non-payment
Operational impossibility
Conduct that prevents safe delivery of the service

sections.title: 9. Package Changes
sections.body:
A package change requires:

Mutual agreement
Written documentation

Changes do not apply retroactively.

sections.title: 10. Jurisdiction
sections.body:
These terms are governed by the law of Spain.

Disputes are resolved by the competent courts.

sections.title: 1. Data Controller
sections.body:
The data controller is Sentinel, a local property representation service operating in Torrevieja and within a 50–70 km radius.

Contact for data protection matters:
Email: sentinelcostablanca@gmail.com

sections.title: 2. Scope of Data Processed
sections.body:
Sentinel processes only data necessary for:

Responding to enquiries sent via the contact form
Conclusion and performance of the package agreement
Invoicing
Online payment processing
Operational communication with the client

Data may include:

Name
Email address
Phone number
Property location
Billing details
Information required in the service onboarding process

Sentinel does not process data for marketing purposes without explicit consent.

sections.title: 3. Legal Basis for Processing
sections.body:
Data is processed on the basis of:

Performance of contract or pre-contractual steps
Legal obligations (e.g. accounting)
Legitimate interest of the controller (operational communication)
User consent (where applicable)

sections.title: 4. Data Retention
sections.body:
Data is retained:

For the duration of the engagement
For periods required by law (e.g. accounting records)
Until withdrawal of consent, where processing is based on consent

After the required periods, data is deleted or anonymised.

sections.title: 5. Online Payments
sections.body:
For online payments, transaction data is processed by external payment service providers.

Sentinel does not store full payment card data.

Payment providers act as independent data controllers under their own terms.

sections.title: 6. Cookies
sections.body:
The site may use:

Technical cookies (necessary for the site to function)
Functional cookies
Analytics cookies (if enabled)

Users may manage cookies via browser settings.

Disabling some cookies may affect site functionality.

sections.title: 7. User Rights
sections.body:
Users have the right to:

Access their data
Rectification of data
Erasure of data
Restriction of processing
Data portability
Object to processing
Withdraw consent at any time

Requests should be sent to the controller's email address.

sections.title: 8. Data Sharing
sections.body:
Data may be disclosed to:

Accounting service providers
Payment providers
Technology partners operating the site infrastructure

Data is not sold or shared for marketing purposes.

sections.title: 9. Security
sections.body: Sentinel applies appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect data against unauthorised access, loss or disclosure.

sections.title: 10. Policy Changes
sections.body: The Privacy Policy may be updated following legal or operational changes. The current version is published on the site.
